thread.title: Pickerington school board reviews agenda for May 26 business meeting
thread.title_full: Pickerington school board reviews agenda for May 26 business meeting

author: Buckeye Reporter
title: Pickerington school board reviews agenda for May 26 business meeting
text:
The Pickerington Local School District Board of Education held its regular business meeting on May 26 at the district office located at 90 N. East Street, Pickerington. The session began at 6:00 p.m. and included routine business items, presentations, public participation, and updates from district leadership.
The agenda featured a presentation from Woolpert Consultants about the district’s attendance boundary redistricting planning process and an update from Food Services. The board also allowed time for public participation as outlined in Board Policy 0169.1, which requires attendees to register their intention to speak upon arrival and limits each statement to three minutes unless extended by the presiding officer.
Superintendent updates and the Treasurer’s Report followed, including review of previous meeting minutes and acknowledgment of donations. The consent agenda was presented for approval with items such as personnel recommendations, supplemental contracts, early graduation requests, and recognition of Class of 2026 graduates.
Discussion and possible action items included Ohio High School Athletic Association membership renewal, an Academic Services contract, amendments to elementary and middle school fees for the upcoming year, consideration of a Bluum quote for Newline panels technology purchases, resolutions regarding reductions in force (RIFs) affecting certificated employee contracts both fully or partially, as well as an addendum to teacher contracts. The board also conducted a first reading on several new or revised job descriptions including positions such as Supervisor – Accounting; Board Certified Behavior Analyst; Director of Food Services; Food Service Supervisor; Administrative Assistant to the Assistant Superintendent; Paraprofessional (Kindergarten/Title I); and Paraprofessional (ISS).
Informational updates were provided regarding summer camps—including Lady Tigers Basketball Camp scheduled June 8-10 for grades three through eight at Pickerington Central High School Main Gym—and Little Tiger Football Camp set for July 20-22 at Pickerington Central Field House for grades one through eight. An overnight trip was approved for Pickerington High School North Varsity Girls Golf team traveling to Sandusky on August 12-13 with funding provided by boosters and parents rather than district funds.
Graduate program applications were acknowledged, including one from Nancy Gdovin—a third grade teacher at Fairfield Elementary—who plans to pursue a Master of Science in Curriculum and Instruction from Western Governors University over two years. The meeting concluded with comments or questions from both the public and board members before adjournment.
